title: Session TTL + Compact-Worker runtime hotfix for cross-region memory skew and KV ghost allocations
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported recurrent GPU OOMs and severe tail latency correlated with long-lived sessions pinned to single shards in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Investigation shows a combination of stale session allocations (ghost entries in the KV layer) and slab fragmentation that prevented background compaction from reclaiming space under standard heuristics, causing slot starvation during traffic bursts. This ticket tracks the runtime patch that introduces a session TTL eviction policy and a controlled compact-worker that runs under explicit memory pressure thresholds, plus associated observability and rollout plan.

2026-02-25 05:40 UTC: Dedicated customer support ticket reported SLA breaches for inference endpoints; attached heap profiles and allocation samples.
2026-02-26 11:00 UTC: Private deployment (on-prem) customer reported similar behavior after a canary model rollout; logs show long-lived KV handles linked to inactive sessions.
2026-02-26 14:30 UTC: Paging incident declared. Mitigation: increased autoscale headroom for affected pools and temporary eviction of low-priority tenants.
2026-02-27 09:00 UTC: Root cause hypothesis formed: session-affinity + missing TTL + compactor backoff leads to ghost allocations and fragmentation.
2026-03-01 10:00 UTC: ENG-100030 created to implement deterministic solution (session TTL + compact-worker) and reduce blast radius for runtime patches.
2026-03-03 16:00 UTC: Patch branch opened and initial unit tests added; perf bench started against synthetic long-lived session workload.

2026-03-09 23:00 UTC: Canary metrics show 78% reduction in tail OOMs and steady compactor throughput without latency regressions.

root_cause_summary: Long-lived session handles were retained indefinitely when clients used sticky routing to a shard. The runtime's background compaction backoff logic treated heavily fragmented slabs as low-priority and delayed reclamation. Combined with sudden traffic bursts, this produced slot starvation on GPUs and OOMs. KV layer retained small ghost allocations that prevented contiguous free spans from forming for large tensor allocations.
temporary_mitigations: Increase autoscaling headroom for affected GPU pools (hosted and dedicated)
Manual eviction of low-priority sessions for impacted tenants during incident window
Restart affected private clusters with aggressive slab reclaim flags as emergency measure
proposed_fix_summary: Implement session TTL with configurable default (30m) and tenant-overrides, and add a compact-worker that triggers when free_contiguous_bytes < threshold OR ghost_allocation_ratio > threshold. The compact-worker runs in small adjustable batches and yields to inference workers to avoid latency spikes. Add metrics for ghost_allocation_ratio, compact_worker_cycles, session_ttl_evictions and a new alert when compact cycles > X/min.
dashboards: Runtime / Memory / Ghost Allocation Ratio (dashboard id: db-rt-mem-09)

regression_risks: Compact-worker could interfere with latency-sensitive inference if not rate-limited
Session TTL might cause unexpected session churn for some long-running customer workflows
Tenant-specific overrides misconfiguration could lead to premature evictions
qa_plan: Unit tests for session TTL enforcement, edge cases where sessions are actively writing to KV
Integration test that simulates sticky session traffic with long-lived connections and verifies compaction reclaims memory without increasing p95 latency > 5%
Load test on dedicated pool with mixed tenants to validate tenant-overrides and canary config
Security review of configuration flags and RBAC exposure (config can only be changed by ops/admin roles)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Merge PRs and run CI pipeline (smoke + unit + integration)
Stage 1: Deploy telemetry-only agent to production for 24h to validate metrics (no behavioral changes)
Stage 2: Canary deploy to single Dedicated pool (eu-central-1) for 48h with session-ttl=30m and compact-worker in passive mode
Stage 3: If canary stable, enable compact-worker active mode in Hosted burst pools and monitor for 72h
Stage 4: Full rollout to all Dedicated and Private clusters with tenant overrides and operator runbooks
rollback_plan: Disable compact-worker via runtime flag (fast) and revert session_ttl to previous behaviour via config rollback
If rollback insufficient, redeploy previous runtime image (previous stable tag)
Communicate to customers and restore autoscale headroom while investigation continues
postmortem_actions: Add automated mem-pressured canary that simulates ghost allocations in CI
Product: document tenant-runbook for long-lived session use cases and recommended configuration
Engineering: add a background compaction budget gauge and an automated remediation playbook
Observability: create alert on ghost_allocation_ratio > 5% for > 10m
Release: include runtime-1.2.7-hotfix release notes and customer-facing KB article
